preamble: Raising of the nasalized mid back vowel [õ] to [ũ], favoured because nasal coupling blurs perceived vowel height (F1). Basque shows two related processes: in Souletin (Zuberoan), stressed word-final /õ/ regularly raised to /ũ/ (ardũ 'wine' vs. standard ardo); separately, phonetically nasalized [õ] next to a nasal consonant raised irregularly in the eastern dialects, chiefly Souletin and Roncalese (hun 'good' vs. on). No comparable case outside Basque has been verified.

examples.note: Regular raising of stressed word-final /õ/ to /ũ/ in Souletin; likewise arratũ 'rat' (cf. arratoi), arrazũ 'reason' (cf. arrazoi), salũ 'living room' (cf. saloi).
Irregular raising of phonetically nasalized [õ] beside a nasal consonant, also in hunat 'hither' (cf. hona), khuntü 'account' (cf. kontu); found chiefly in Souletin and Roncalese.

sources: Egurtzegi, A. (2013). Ekialdeko /o/-ren igoeraren testuinguru fonologikoaren bila / Looking for the phonological context of /o/-raising in Eastern Basque. Anuario del Seminario de Filología Vasca 'Julio de Urquijo' 47(2): 257–266. https://doi.org/10.1387/asju.18683
